title: Retrieving 3D Atomic Coordinates of 2D Materials using Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: When layers of 2D materials are stacked with an interlayer twist, their atomic structure undergoes in-plane and out-of-plane deformation as a function of local stacking order, thereby altering the electronic structure [1]. Precise experimental characterization of the atomic structure of twisted 2D bilayers is important to understanding their properties. While the in-plane deformations have been studied through diffraction and direct imaging techniques [2,3], the out-of-plane deformations are harder to detect experimentally. Scanning tunneling microscopy can measure surface topography but is limited to the topmost layer of atoms. Electron tomography has been applied to 2D materials [4], but it requires aligning images taken from multiple sample orientations, which is difficult when the sample is extended and very periodic. Here, we experimentally confirm the presence of periodic out-of-plane deformations of twisted bilayer WSe2 using 3D atomic coordinates obtained via multislice electron ptychography.
